GROK BOT HOW TO USE

WHAT NEW TODAY
- Folder now 762 posts (7 new since Aug 29)
- Official bot: improved X support — connect your X profile and a developer account is auto-created with included credits https://t.co/NBucim48w4
- Testers (Teslaconomics): SpaceXAI/cursor_ai clearance — 50 Grok Bot codes now worth $200 each (Ultra plan or on-demand usage); reply with the job you'd give a Bot https://t.co/V1sz9loLeQ
- Testers (Teslaconomics): shocked demand; Grok Bot feels like a major winning product / new category for SpaceX https://t.co/LyksRAYmKv
- Testers quoting SpaceXAI (cb_doge): Grok Bot surpassed OpenClaw in YouTube search interest by a wide margin https://t.co/Ow7S9PFttY
- Testers (niccruzpatane): Accounting Bot (invoices/spending/bills), Personal Bot (flights, rides, Airbnb, Google Calendar, Amazon orders/returns), Home Bot (lights/robots/speakers/thermostats); train it like a human https://t.co/5MqKFcyTWf
- Testers / SpaceXAI (kiaraplds): flights, tickets, groceries — anything you need to delegate can be safely handled by your Bot https://t.co/F2CdZWDhyZ
- Testers (antpalkin): trading-desk build — every agent's job ends with what it may never do without asking; one Bot whose only job is killing bad trades, and its no beats the desk https://t.co/ag4gqRYlZN

WHAT IT IS
- A Bot is a named, persistent teammate, not a one-off chat
- You message it like a coworker and it finishes work in real apps
- All of your Bots share one cloud computer (browser, files, terminal)
- Each Bot has its own screen on that shared computer
- Work keeps going when your laptop or the app is closed
- It only comes back when it needs approval or a human step
- Do not confuse Grok Bot with Digital Optimus (real-time video human emulation)
- Testers (joehansen): do not confuse Grok Bot with an X Chat Agent (an X account you add to a group chat). Grok Bot is the machine that does the work

ACCESS AND INSTALL
- Official bot (Aug 26): All SuperGrok and Cursor Pro subscribers now have access
- Testers quoting SpaceXAI (cb_doge): SuperGrok, SuperGrok Plus, SuperGrok Heavy, Cursor Pro, Cursor Pro+, Cursor Ultra, Cursor Teams Standard and Premium
- Cursor CEO Michael Truell: everyone with a standard Grok or Cursor subscription
- Testers: included at no extra cost with those plans; circulating plan prices $20/month Cursor Pro and $25/month SuperGrok (nextbigfuture)
- Official bot + Elon: weekly / free usage limits reset for all Grok Bot users
- Sign in with your Cursor account (that account owns plan and usage)
- Official desktop download: https://t.co/tHvaZ7icnr
- Also listed at https://t.co/bfJPYFHLZz
- Official desktop is macOS and Windows (Apple silicon or Intel; Windows x64 or Arm64)
- Official docs say Linux desktop is not currently available
- iPhone: iOS 18+, App Store app "Grok Bot"
- Official docs still say iPad and Android are not supported yet for actual use
- Grok Bot team (poteto, Aug 27): Android app almost ready; pre-register on Google Play https://t.co/o7XKDJuWcv
- Testers quoting SpaceXAI (cb_doge): Android app available for pre-registration on Google Play
- SuperGrok Heavy users can choose Get access with SuperGrok Heavy, then Link Grok Account
- Linking SuperGrok Heavy can unlock free Cursor Ultra (one Grok account to one Cursor account)
- Legacy Privacy Mode blocks Grok Bot; switch to a supported Cursor data setting first
- Grok Bot checks for updates automatically; Check for Updates is in Settings → Beta
- Bookmark testers: iPad may be coming soon; official docs still say iPad is not supported yet

SIGN IN
- Desktop: Get started, then Sign In with Cursor in the browser
- iOS: Login with Cursor, finish in the browser, return to the app
- Official: Cmd-D turns on voice dictation
- Official: it is easier to use the remote computer from your phone
- Use the same Cursor account that should own usage
- First-run tour asks which tools you use; that only shapes teammate suggestions
- Computer setup runs in the background, then Meet a future teammate opens

CREATE A BOT
- New in the sidebar, or Cmd/Ctrl+N
- In New chat, choose Create new agent
- Edit Profile: name, title, description, avatar
- Give a short name, one primary job, and how it should work
- Description = standing rules (never send without approval)
- Chat messages = this-task instructions (draft follow-ups for these 12 accounts)
- Focused Bots beat one catch-all General Helper
- Bookmark testers: start with about six roles; give each Bot recurring work
- Pin important Bots; hide unused ones (hiding does not pause routines)
- Bookmark testers: resize the sidebar, give titles, and group Bots into sections
- Duplicate a Bot to reuse a role for a new scope (copy does not include memory or history)
- Delete only if you are sure; files and logins on the shared computer stay
- Account limit: 50 Bots and group chats combined
- Name language can steer reply language (bookmark testers reported this)
- Bookmark testers: no model picker yet; testers still list voice mode, BYOK, multiplayer, hang-error messages, and a real iPad app as missing

HOW TO WRITE A TASK
- Outcome: what should be finished
- Sources: which apps, sites, files, or chats matter
- Constraints: what it must not do, or must ask first
- Deliverable: what it should return
- Review point: when it should stop for you
- Safe first task: attach a file and ask for a cited summary; do not change the file
- Next task: one real tool, read-only, with a sign-in handoff if needed
- After a good result, name the lasting format preference in chat
- Then save it as a skill or routine
- Official bot examples: email cleanup, Starlink-likely flights, build a site then buy the domain and deploy, meeting notes, sales prospecting, refunds, podcast audio digest
- Testers: paste a viral video link and ask the Bot to recreate it
- Testers: start from an org chart or make one Bot the boss of a repo, not a long to-do list
- Testers: one clear job, explicit allowed sources, no-guessing rule, approval gate before any real action
- Testers: 5 calibrations — confidence threshold, checkpoint long tasks, show negative examples, gate destructive actions separately, test edge cases first
- Testers: one Bot, one job — two jobs claimed worse at both; put recurring work on a schedule
- Testers quoting claimed SpaceXAI employee: version prompts and tool configs like code; scratchpad separate from the user-facing answer; retry with a different strategy; measure cost per successful outcome; review failure logs on a schedule
- Testers (mvanhorn): Compound Engineering — force a plan first; three-layer instructions (base, role, current focus); screenshot instead of retyping what's on screen; ping only on a real hit
- Testers (AlexFinn): anything you are about to do on your computer, ask Grok Bot first
- Testers (AlexFinn): example week — Reddit microSaaS, 3D digital office to watch Bots, Omarchy setup, product returns, daily AI news post, Cursor cloud-agent bug fixes, X model-release watch, brand-deal negotiation, contract redlines

AGENT COMPUTER AND LOGINS
- Open Agent Computer from the conversation to watch the desktop
- Take over for password, passkey, 2FA, CAPTCHA, payment, or human-only pages
- Complete only the blocked step, then return control
- Never paste passwords or one-time codes into chat
- Use a secure secret request when the app offers one
- Browser sessions persist and are shared across all your Bots
- Prefer a connector/plugin when one exists; use the browser when it does not
- Keep durable files in /workspace with clear project folders
- Settings → Beta: Update Agent Computer (preserve state), Recover, or Reset (can lose recent work)
- The cloud computer is not your Mac or Windows machine
- Local-computer execution is separate: Settings → General → Agent → Execution on Local Computer
- Default local policy is Ask every time; use Never allowed unless you need local files
- Bookmark testers: give a Bot full local Mac/iMessage access only on a spare machine
- Testers: local Mac access can write local Python scripts on your Mac
- Testers (Av1dlive / mvanhorn): Claude Code, Codex, and Cursor claimed runnable on the Bot's own computer
- Testers (XFreeze): take over that same cloud computer from your phone without being at the laptop
- Testers (AlexFinn): a 3D digital office on a second monitor to watch Bots work

PLUGINS AND CONNECTORS
- Settings → Plugins, then Add, then authenticate in the browser
- Type  to attach a connector; type / to reference a saved skill
- Installed connectors are account-wide, not isolated to one Bot
- Official: you can connect multiple accounts to the same plugin
- Official bot (Aug 26): SuperGrok and Cursor Pro now included; weekly limits reset. Testers quoting SpaceXAI: also Plus/Heavy/Pro+/Ultra/Teams
- Testers: give a Bot its own email address so it can send and receive on its own
- Testers (mvanhorn): give a Bot its own inbox, not your Gmail (one mistake should not flag your domain); Twilio number so a Bot can make calls
- Testers: app v0.23.0 adds creating new channels
- Official bot: improved X support — connect your X profile; a developer account is auto-created with included credits https://t.co/NBucim48w4
- Follow the Connect card when a Bot asks for a plugin
- Bookmark testers: X connector may still need a paid X API key in some setups (official path now auto-creates a developer account with credits)
- Bookmark testers: image generation works; testers now also claim video editing (music sync). Video generation still unconfirmed. Testers (XFreeze): dedicated video-editor Bot for footage → clips/cuts/sound/titles
- Bookmark testers: Grok Bot can now read your X bookmarks
- Testers (testerlabor): you can link your X Premium+ subscription to Grok Bot
- Testers: Higgsfield x Grok Bot; 100 free credits for new users
- Testers: send a YouTube link with start/end timestamps and get an HD clip in chat (Google login claimed)
- Testers: give a Bot Grok Build + Cursor CLI so weekly limits can be spread across Cursor and Grok

SKILLS AND ROUTINES
- Skill = reusable how-to (steps, rules, output, approval boundary)
- Routine = when to run that work (schedule or event)
- Do the task once, make it reliable, save a skill, then automate
- Teach a task: open computer view, choose Teach a task, demo up to 10 minutes, review the draft skill
- Teaching records the screen, not microphone audio; do not expose secrets while teaching
- If Teach a task is missing, ask the Bot to write a skill from the completed work
- Create a routine on the Bot that should own the job
- Confirm owner, schedule, time zone, input, result, approval, and missing-data behavior
- Event triggers (Slack, GitHub) are separate from plugins and need their own connection
- Keep event matchers narrow; avoid every new message
- Test run does real work; use safe inputs
- Testers quoting docs: Test can send real emails to real clients; Stop is a brake, not a rewind
- View conversation details → Routines to pause, edit, inspect, or delete
- A Bot can own 50 routines; last 20 run records are kept
- Deleting a routine has no undo
- Testers quoting docs: delete a Bot and every routine on it dies; no undo
- Long absence can pause unattended routines until you confirm
- Bookmark testers: Teach a task from + in the browser, record yourself, then let the Bot replay it
- Testers: skills taught to one bot claimed available across the account team on the same computer
- Testers: shareable templates claimed coming — package a Bot, share link, one-click add
- Testers: a reusable-skills source claimed (BrianRoemmele)
- Testers quoting Grok Bot team (0xMorlex): keep recurring routines off the main agent's context
- Testers (mvanhorn): Teach by recording and respect the 10-minute cap

MULTI BOT TEAMS
- Start with one Bot that owns an end-to-end outcome
- Add a specialist only when the role is stable
- Use a group chat when the handoff itself should be visible
- Bots can message each other and pass ownership
- Do not treat separate Bots as a security boundary (they share the computer)
- Keep sending, buying, deleting, publishing, and production changes behind approval
- Bookmark testers: a Bot may create other Bots before it can delete them
- Bookmark testers: tell a hub Bot to loop a specialist every few minutes and watch it
- Testers: put Bots in one group chat, appoint a Chief of Staff, and stop being the router
- Testers: isolate each Bot's job and add a supervisor; a crew without that can perform worse
- Testers: night-shift crews (chief, scout, forge, critic, ship, ledger) share one computer; human gate for merge, production, spend, send, delete
- Testers: one group chat per job/post, not per Bot; you only message the Chief of Staff
- Testers: show the workflow once on screen rather than writing a long spec
- Testers: add a RED TEAM Bot whose job is to disprove the thesis; no single source closes a claim
- Testers quoting Grok Bot team (0xMorlex): specialist roles (designer/engineer/PM); organize projects without a new Bot for everything; a Chief of Agents that creates and manages the rest
- Testers (mvanhorn): Bot Advisor whose only job is building and tightening other Bots; files are the memory bus between Bots

IOS
- Same Bots, chats, routines, plugins, and cloud computer as desktop
- Send text, dictate, attach photos/files, mention Bots, reply in threads
- Take over the computer for login/2FA from the phone
- You can pause or resume a routine on iOS
- Editing schedule, run history, test, delete, and teach-by-demo still need desktop
- Enable notifications for results, questions, and approvals
- Testers: phone notification shows the proposed action; approve or deny
- Testers (XFreeze): you can operate and take over the Bot's computer from your phone as long as it has internet
- Grok Bot team (poteto): Android app in Google Play pre-registration, not shipping yet. Official docs still say Android is not supported

APPROVALS AND SAFETY
- Put the stop line in the request: draft, do not send; ask after showing current vs proposed
- Desktop: Allow once, Deny, or Always allow a matching rule
- iPhone: Approve once or Deny
- Auto Review: Settings → General → Auto-review
- Require Approval beats Always Allow when both match
- Write narrow rules, not allow everything in the browser
- Do not approve an action you cannot identify
- Connect only the tools the workflow needs
- Start read-only; keep spend, send, publish, delete, and production behind approval
- Sign out and revoke connectors when access should end
- Deleting a Bot does not wipe shared files or browser sessions
- Bookmark testers: delay standing inbox/CRM access until you trust the beta
- Bookmark testers: one person burned a 7-day quota in about 8 hours
- Bookmark testers: SuperGrok may offer one-off usage resets in settings; use before they expire
- Testers: gate destructive actions (delete, overwrite, irreversible send) as their own confirmation, not lumped with routine tool use
- Testers quoting docs: Test run does real work; Stop does not unsend
- Testers quoting Elon (cb_doge): connecting a Bot to a bank account; Elon said any loss from a bot mistake would be covered. Still keep spend behind approval
- Official bot Link shopping: keep purchases behind approval even though the Bot can complete them on your behalf
- Testers (mvanhorn): unsupervised crews claimed to multiply their own errors ~17x; draft-then-approve anything that sends; most Bots that don't own an outcome fail
- Testers (antpalkin): end every agent's job with a hard never-without-asking list; give one Bot veto/kill power whose no beats the rest of the desk

FIRST BOTS WORTH CREATING
- Inbox manager for email and Slack triage
- Calendar and reservation Bot
- Research and daily brief Bot
- Coding Bot that can launch Cursor cloud agents
- Chief-of-staff hub that routes work to specialists
- Personal errands Bot (tickets, food, travel, forms)
- Content Bot that drafts in your voice for approval
- Chief-of-staff that researches you, organizes the other Bots, and can turn the digest into a morning podcast
- Testers (mvanhorn): Bot Advisor; own-inbox Bot; a call Bot with its own number
- Testers (techdevnotes): default Bots circulating — Night Shift (overnight digest), Inbox Triage, Chief of Staff, Negotiator, Prototyper, Researcher, Shopper, Apartment Scout, Lookout, Competitor Watcher
- Testers (techdevnotes): also tool-specific sales/ops/dev roles (CRM scribe, pipeline scout, ticket triager, QA, dashboard watcher)
- Official bot + Link: Shopper Bot can now complete online purchases once link is connected (keep approval on)
- Testers / SpaceXAI (kiaraplds): flights, tickets, groceries — delegate errands safely to your Bot
- Testers (minchoi): one-person-company setups — money, appointments, running ops from the phone
- Testers (niccruzpatane): Accounting Bot (invoices, spending, bills); Personal Bot (flights, rides, Airbnb, Google Calendar, Amazon orders/returns); Home Bot (lights, robots, speakers, thermostats)

TESLA OPTIMUS

NEW TODAY
- Merged 254 unique (Optimus 251 + academy 3, overlap 0); 2 new vs yesterday (252)
- Testers (stevenmarkryan): • More Big Tesla Robotaxi Developments • Big Hint Tesla Optimus Will Blow Your Mind • "OpenAI" Has Public Meltdown Over Elon Musk • Elon Cl…
- Testers (darrennn (genzzztrade)): Jcal reveals Elon showed him insane unreleased Tesla Optimus footage "I saw the latest Optimus. He's making sick progress. He's not showing…

WHAT IT IS
- Tesla’s general-purpose humanoid robot. Official accounts in this dump: Tesla and Tesla_Optimus. Physical robot + academy/training bookmarks — not Digital Optimus.
- Elon: first humanoid meant to do generalized useful work in factories and homes — not a pre-programmed demo. Built about 5'11", with human-level (or better) hand dexterity.
- Elon: “It won't even seem like a robot. It'll seem like a human in a robot suit.” You’ll have to poke it to believe it’s real.
- Testers: Tesla vehicles and Optimus share the same cameras, computers, and batteries. Testers quoting Tesla Newswire: two eyes, same cameras as Tesla cars.
- Generations in this dump: Gen 2 / 2.5 (current demos, running, factory tests); Gen 3 (first mass-production design); then Optimus 4 and 5 on an annual cycle. Aug 24 tester (maksim434244): Gen 3 body 57 kg / 173 cm, lighter on purpose.

HOW IT WORKS
- Elon: learn a task by watching a human, hearing a verbal description, or watching a video — no step-by-step programming. “No one's ever achieved this.”
- Elon: most impressive internet humanoid demos are pre-programmed or remotely controlled. No current humanoid does generalized tasks. That is the Optimus goal.
- Official Tesla_Optimus (Dec 2025): “Just set a new PR in the lab.” Testers: walks on end-to-end neural nets trained in simulation. Elon confirmed some clips (kung fu, running) were AI-driven end to end.
- Hands: testers quoting Elon / engineers — 22 degrees of freedom; actuators moved out of the palm into the forearm with cable-tendons. Elon: forearm and hand are ~60% of the engineering difficulty. Testers: lift about 40 lb and still not crush an egg. Aug 23–24 tester (maksim434244): Gen 3 hands 22 DoF, 25 actuators each / 50 across both arms (old hands had 11); synthetic tendons; egg without breaking the yolk. Academy tester (0xOracul): catch/reopen practice as the home-robot hand skill.
- Testers (Aug 23): some early units still VR-teleop driven while the robot watches and learns; one Miami anecdote of a unit falling when headset control released — treat as tester caution on autonomy readiness.
- Testers: AI5 is the on-device chip (testers quoting Elon on tape-out, Apr 2026). Aug 24 tester (maksim434244): AI5 “40 times faster”; Grok handles language/reasoning, Tesla vision networks handle the body. That split is a tester claim, not Official Tesla.
- Testers: Tesla patented a “universal cortex” so Optimus inherits the car’s camera perception stack. Knee patent: 4-bar linkage, about 150° of bend.
- Leadership (tester, Aug 23): Milan Kovac left Jun 2025 after ~9 years on Optimus; Ashok Elluswamy (FSD software) now owns the program — tester read: hardware landed, software is the bottleneck.

ACADEMY / TRAINING
- Testers brand Elon’s sim-to-real self-play plan “Optimus Academy” (training for the robot, not a separate consumer product / not Digital Optimus). Academy bookmark folder still 3 posts (unchanged Aug 27).
- Elon via testers (Dwarkesh, also in Optimus folder): tens of thousands of robots (at least 10,000, maybe 20–30,000) doing self-play to close the sim-to-real gap.
- Academy folder (the_latticex): millions of virtual robots practice in physics-accurate simulations while 10,000–30,000 physical Optimus units test those skills in the real world; every attempt becomes training data; fleet can copy a mastered skill.
- Academy tester (0xOracul): catch/reopen practice as the home-robot hand skill.
- Academy tester (XFreeze): short clip — “Sustainable, abundant and autonomous.”
- Testers: Cortex 2 training compute for the Optimus model. Elon via testers (Mar 2026): first half of Cortex 2 to go live in April.
- Early physical units: stay inside Tesla for teleop/learn (~1k built this year / sell zero — tester Aug 23). Aug 24 tester: first robots off the line go into Tesla’s own factories to train each other. Academy hand-catch clips are practice demos, not a shippable home product.

HOW TO USE / ACCESS
- Not for sale. You cannot buy one from anything in this folder. Early units stay inside Tesla for testing and data.
- Official Tesla (Nov 2025): pilot production line running in Fremont; testing in factories and office spaces for real-time use cases.
- Elon (Feb 2026): “By the end of 2027, I think we'd be selling humanoid robots to the public, That's when we are confident that it's very high reliability, very high safety, and the range of functionality is also very high. You can basically ask it to do anything.”
- Testers (Jul 2026 app-code dive): Tesla app adding home-data consent (video, 3D spatial, tactile), a Bluetooth robot key with a device whitelist, and simple owner alerts (low battery, mechanical issue). Tester leak, not an Official Tesla post.
- Testers: Tesla is hiring for Optimus Simulation (Palo Alto) plus 172–208 Optimus-labeled jobs (Palo Alto, Fremont, Austin, Langley BC, Athens). Watch Tesla careers, not a storefront.

PRODUCTION / FACTORY
- Official Tesla (Nov 6, 2025): Fremont pilot line is running. “Significantly larger Gen 3 production line coming in 2026.”
- Tesla via testers (Jan 2026): Gen 3 is the first design meant for mass production. Start of production planned before the end of 2026. Eventual planned capacity 1 million robots per year.
- Elon (Abundance Summit, Mar 2026): start Optimus 3 production “this summer, but very slow at first,” high-volume around summer 2027. Then Optimus 4 the next year. Annual new design.
- Elon (his post, Jan 29, 2026): “Optimus 4 will be built in Texas at much higher volume.”
- Elon (Jul 2026): Fremont S/X floor is being converted to the Optimus line. “There is no supply chain.” Hardest product Tesla has ever tried to scale. Everything is new. Testers quoting the Q2 call: initial ramp “quite flat and long.”
- Elon on the V3 show (Apr 2026): push the unveil closer to production (late July / August) because competitors do frame-by-frame copies. This dump has no Official V3 launch post after that window.
- Testers (Aug 24, maksim434244): Model S assembly line torn down in 46 days for Optimus; 10,000 unique parts; Tesla building the supply chain from zero. First units stay inside Tesla factories.
- Testers (Aug 25, JoeTegtmeyer): Giga Texas Optimus factory weekly timelapse, ~5 months in; his estimate 6–8 months still to assemble the full structure — not producing yet.
- Testers (Aug 24, OverlyTrev): Texas site ~10M/year at full ramp and meant for Optimus 4; guesses Optimus 3 before year-end as Fremont comes online.
- Testers (Aug 23–24): ~1,000 built this year / sell zero (internal training); Polymarket ~9% odds of 2026 commercial launch (down from ~33%) — timeline skepticism, not “robot failed.” CapEx chatter >$25B across AI/Robotaxi/Optimus in 2026.
- Unconfirmed / media (Aug 21–23): Gen 2 pilot chatter at Giga Berlin (battery area, shielded zones). Leave commercial Berlin claims unconfirmed.

CONFLICT — volume and factory size
- Official / Elon: start late 2026, slow ramp, 1M/year Fremont capacity eventually; high volume ~summer 2027; Texas is the much-higher-volume (Optimus 4) site. Testers repeat 1M Fremont + 10M Texas; one Aug 23 tester says 11M+/year at scale. Aug 25 tester (niccruzpatane) uses 10M at $20–25k to get $200–250B/year — tester math.
- Older testers (Jan 2026): Chinese-supply “mass production audit,” $685M order with seven Tier-1s, 50,000–100,000 units by end of 2026. Jul 2026 testers quoting Shanghai VP Tao Lin: Jul–Aug start, Q4 10,000/month, 50–100k in 2026 then 500k–1M in 2027. Those 2026 unit counts sit well above Elon’s “very slow at first” line and above Aug 23 “~1k built / sell zero” tester framing. Do not pick a winner.
- Factory-size testers also disagree: about 5.2 million sq ft North Campus vs 8 million sq ft.

PRICE / PLANS
- Official Tesla (Nov 2025): “Our goal is $20k COGS per robot at scale.” That is cost of goods, not a sticker price.
- Elon (All-In, testers Sep 2025): “the marginal cost of production once you hit a million units per year is probably around the $20,000 range.” Depends on the AI chip and actuator efficiency (26 actuators per arm in that quote).
- CONFLICT — price: testers also quote a $20,000–$30,000 public/target price. One Aug 20 tester cites both $20k (Elon “priced it”) and $30k (Musk price target) the same day. Official language in this dump is $20k COGS / ~$20k marginal cost at 1M/year. $30k is tester. Aug 23 tester (maksim434244) cites current unit cost $50k–$100k — early/low-volume chatter, not Official COGS. Aug 24 same tester restates $20–30k target vs $150–250k competitors.
- Elon: public sales targeted end of 2027. Testers repeat that. Prediction-market odds of a 2026 commercial launch are low (~9% Polymarket, tester).
- Elon: demand guess “20 billion-ish” — at least one per person plus industry. Ron Baron via testers (Jul 2026): Musk talking past 10 million to 100 million then a billion. Those are demand visions, not orders.
- Elon via testers (shareholder meeting): Optimus 4 production 2027, Optimus 5 2028. One Aug 21 tester repeats Gen 4 2027 / Gen 5 2028.
- Elon: “Optimus is kind of like an infinite money glitch.” Future value “might be measured in terms of wattage.”

JOBS / TASKS
- Official Tesla: already testing real-time use cases in factories and offices. Testers (Mar 2026): units doing useful work at Giga Texas and Giga Nevada — moving parts, sorting, repetitive assembly. Treat factory-work claims as tester unless Official. Aug 23–24 testers: internal-first deployment before customer sales.
- Elon: 24-hour nurse/helper; dangerous or repetitive work first. Walk the dog, take care of the house, babysit, teach kids, cook dinner, play the piano. Fine motor control “suitable for medical and manufacturing environments.”
- Elon (Jan 2026 clip + Aug 20–21 restated): robot doctors / better than the best human surgeon in about three years. Testers date that to ~2029. Elon’s prediction, not a medical product on sale.
- Elon: law-enforcement idea — a free Optimus that follows a person and stops crime (“more humane form of containment”). No weapons in that quote.
- Testers listing Tesla video chores: vacuum, fetch a paper towel, water a plant, dishes, iron, cabinets, clean a table, whiteboard, open/close curtains, set up a party, put a pan on a stove.
- Testers (Aug 24, veloraaivs / nexoraAIxt): home pitch as many small chores (car vacuum, upstairs, plants, laundry, kitchen, errands) and hard fine-motor tasks (matching socks); cooking-dinner clip framed as care/home-life, not a shippable product.
- Tester speculation (Shred_0x, Aug 23): hotel housekeeping split across two humanoids by summer 2027 (China/UAE chain confirmation bet) — prediction, not Official Tesla.

SAFETY
- Elon: must be extremely reliable before public sale. A ~70 kg robot that “flopped over” has to be carried out “like a body.” “We don't want Optimus to go haywire.”
- Elon: wait for “very high reliability, very high safety” — his end-2027 public-sale condition.
- Testers: home units would be cameras on legs. App leak claims a Bluetooth key whitelist so the robot ignores unauthorized phones.
- Testers: Elon said some demos (kung fu, running) were end-to-end AI; he has not said which other demos used a motion-capture human. Do not treat every clip as unsupervised autonomy. Aug 23 tester: Miami fall when teleop released — reinforces “not unsupervised yet.”

USEFUL WORKFLOWS
- Do not try to buy one. Public sales are an end-2027 Elon target, not a checkout page. 2026 commercial-launch odds in this dump are market-skeptical.

🤔 Can reinforcement learning teach diffusion models how every denoising step should improve, instead of only rewarding the final generated image?

𝗗𝗶𝗳𝗳𝘂𝘀𝗶𝗼𝗻𝗢𝗣𝗦𝗗: 𝗢𝗻-𝗣𝗼𝗹𝗶𝗰𝘆 𝗦𝗲𝗹𝗳-𝗗𝗶𝘀𝘁𝗶𝗹𝗹𝗮𝘁𝗶𝗼𝗻 𝗶𝗻 𝗗𝗶𝗳𝗳𝘂𝘀𝗶𝗼𝗻 𝗠𝗼𝗱𝗲𝗹𝘀

Recent diffusion RL methods optimize image-level rewards, yet diffusion models generate images through hundreds of intermediate denoising predictions. This creates a fundamental supervision gap:

How can endpoint rewards effectively guide intermediate denoising steps?

In 𝗗𝗶𝗳𝗳𝘂𝘀𝗶𝗼𝗻𝗢𝗣𝗦𝗗, we introduce On-Policy Self-Distillation (OPSD), a new diffusion post-training paradigm that converts image-level reward guidance into explicit intermediate supervision. Reward-guided targets are constructed at sampled denoising queries and continuously refreshed as the policy evolves.

More importantly, we show that target construction and finite optimization are fundamentally different problems—a target with higher reward improvement does not necessarily produce a better optimization update. This suggests a new evaluation principle for diffusion RL.

Across SD3.5-M and Z-Image-Turbo, 𝗗𝗶𝗳𝗳𝘂𝘀𝗶𝗼𝗻𝗢𝗣𝗦𝗗 achieves the best held-out performance in 19/20 reward-matched settings, improves over the strongest baseline by up to 44%, and reduces training GPU-hours by 40–63% compared with DiffusionNFT.

We hope this work provides a new perspective on making diffusion post-training both more effective and more interpretable.

Feedback and discussions are very welcome!

"On-Policy Self-Distillation in Diffusion Models"

Diffusion RL gets a reward only after the final image, even though the model actually acts through many intermediate denoising steps.

DiffusionOPSD turns that endpoint reward into explicit reward-improving targets at the model’s own intermediate states, then distills those targets back into the model and continually refreshes them on-policy.

Across two diffusion backbones and ten evaluators, it gets the best held-out score in 19 of 20 settings while cutting training GPU-hours by up to 63%.

The key idea is treating diffusion alignment less like noisy trajectory-level RL and more like continuously refreshed self-distillation with direct intermediate supervision.
